https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026.text: Sarah Williams owned a flat in the Spectrum Building, which burned down while the flammable cladding on the exterior was being replaced. Photograph: Jill Mead/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Sarah Williams owned a flat in the Spectrum Building, which burned down while the flammable cladding on the exterior was being replaced. Photograph: Jill Mead/The Guardian Housing Two years in limbo: the residents still paying mortgages on flats destroyed in east London fire Spectrum Building leaseholders awaiting payouts after freeholder, Arinium, went bankrupt shortly after 2024 blaze Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent Wed 26 Aug 2026 01.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Sarah Williams vividly remembers the night in 2016 when she camped overnight in a car park to put down a deposit on a flat in the newly completed Spectrum Building in Dagenham, east London. “People started queuing for those flats 24 hours before they went on sale,” she said. “It was basically the only flat I could afford in London. This was a year before Grenfell, and the flats market in London was completely crazy.” Four years later, her flat became unsellable when they realised it was covered in dangerous, flammable cladding. Another four years and it, like Grenfell Tower in west London in 2017, had burned down. It has been two years since the fire at the Spectrum Building on 26 August 2024, which left more than 80 people homeless. They were forced to flee a blaze that broke out in the early hours of the morning, fuelled by the scaffolding that covered the building while the cladding was replaced. 1:01 London firefighters tackle blaze at Dagenham tower block – video Williams, like many leaseholders, is stuck in a legal limbo, paying the mortgage on a flat that no longer exists, with no idea how much she will get back. The building’s freeholder, Arinium Ltd, went bankrupt shortly after the fire, and administrators are now responsible for distributing any remaining money, including insurance payouts for loss and damages. “We still haven’t got our money, and we have no idea whether it will even cover the value of the flats,” said Williams, a charity worker. “We don’t know when we’re going to get it. We’ve still got to pay our mortgages. We’ve still got to pay our rent. “So many people have told us: ‘It’s terrible what happened to you, and this is a priority for us.’ But our lives are still on hold.” Insurance payouts are covering emergency accommodation for leaseholders for three years – no one knows what will happen if compensation hasn’t been awarded by then, and people are left to pay both rent and a mortgage. View image in fullscreen James Allchurch lost his own flat and another he rented out in the Spectrum Building fire. Photograph: Antonio Olmos/The Guardian James Allchurch, who owned two flats which burned down in the fire, said the arduous legal process was compounding the trauma many experienced that night. He and his partner ran from their third-floor flat when he woke up by chance and saw embers and blue flashing lights outside the window. “We just grabbed whatever clothes we had and ran out the building, leaving everything behind. Because the last thing you think is, we’ll never go back in our flat,” he said. “It wears you down. I still have nightmares about the fire, I have nightmares about watching our building being demolished, losing everything. There’s an underlying sense of anxiety that has been with me most days since that fire.” View image in fullscreen More than 200 firefighters with 40 fire appliances tackled the blaze in the Spectrum Building in Dagenham. Photograph: Rex/Shutterstock Leaseholders are also concerned that if the freeholder is prosecuted over any fire safety breaches and ultimately fined, that money could come out of the pot of money that would otherwise be distributed to them. “You want some justice, you want to feel that someone’s taking responsibility and there’s accountability,” Allchurch said. “But the result of that might be that we’re all thousands of pounds worse off.” As well as frustration at the delays in getting any money back, residents are angry at what they describe as the painfully slow pace of work to replace flammable cladding on buildings across the country. View image in fullscreen Angela Rayner (centre), the then deputy prime minister, visiting the Spectrum Building after the fire. Photograph: Stefan Rousseau/PA The day after the fire, the then deputy prime minister, Angela Rayner, told reporters at the site that cladding remediation was going “far too slowly” and vowed to “speed up the process”. But the number of buildings in need of cladding remediation where work has started or been completed has only increased from 50% to 53% in the past two years. “I don’t want anybody else to go through this,” said Williams. “Do not stand in front of my smouldering building saying this is a priority then fail to follow up on that. I expected fast and urgent action, but I haven’t seen that for the residents of Spectrum and I haven’t seen that for the country.” Giles Grover, from the End Our Cladding Scandal campaign group, said they were still waiting for Labour to keep its manifesto commitments on building safety. “Progress has been very slow in the last couple of years,” he said. “There’s been a couple of small steps forward, but it’s piecemeal. “It feels like Labour prioritised building 1.5m homes, and that’s meant they’ve swept ending the building safety crisis under the carpet. But this fire was a warning, and they need to heed it. There’s hundreds of thousands of people still living in unsafe buildings.” A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said: “The residents of the Spectrum Building must be fully and urgently compensated so they can start to rebuild their lives – and we urge the building’s administrators to resolve the insurance settlements as quickly as possible. “More broadly, we’re speeding up cladding removal to bring the building safety crisis to an end, and introducing a new legal duty to remediate, to force those responsible to fix unsafe buildings or face criminal prosecution.” Explore more on these topics Housing Greater London Grenfell Tower fire Leasehold Angela Rayner Construction industry Communities news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed Money Property Pensions Savings Borrowing Careers

https://english.news.cn/europe/20260820/.text: Latvian president seeks prosecutor's review after massive data breach RIGA, Aug. 19 (Xinhua) -- Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics has asked the prosecutor general to examine the actions of officials at the Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) over the protection of data following a major cyberattack that exposed information relating to about 1.2 million people. Rinkevics said on Wednesday that the cyberattack and subsequent large-scale data leak amounted to a "scandalous" case, stressing that the issue concerned not only the attack itself but also the responsibility of officials. Transport Minister Rihards Kozlovskis has ordered an expedited internal investigation to establish the circumstances of the attack and determine responsibility. The investigation is also expected to examine CSDD's contract with Latvian technology company Tet for cybersecurity services. Both CSDD's management board and supervisory council decided on Wednesday to step down. According to media reports, the attack took place overnight from Aug. 7 to Aug. 8. Information released after the incident showed that the attackers obtained personal data relating to about 1.2 million individuals and data concerning roughly 200,000 legal entities. The information came from records of payments made to CSDD over the past 18 years. CERT.LV, Cyber incident response institution of Latvia, said preliminary findings indicated that the attack had been targeted and involved advance preparation, while the methods used demonstrated a significant level of technical competence. The agency warned that stolen information could subsequently be used in targeted fraud attempts. Two months earlier, Latvia, a Baltic country with a population of about 1.85 million, experienced another major cybersecurity incident when a large-scale cyberattack against the IT infrastructure of state-owned forestry company Latvijas valsts mezi (LVM) was detected on June 22. CSDD is a state-owned company responsible for vehicle registration, driving licences, vehicle technical inspections and other road traffic services in Latvia. Its state capital shares are held by the Transport Ministry. ■ News In-depth Sports Business Culture World China Regions Asia & Pacific Europe Middle East North America South America Africa Organizations Services Weather Live & Work in China Doing Business Investment Visit China Study in China More Special Reports Photos Video Corrections About Us Contact Us Media Qiushi Journal Taiwan.cn Youth.cn GMW.cn CE.cn Ecns.cn China Daily CRI.cn China.org.cn People's Daily

Simplicius Lithuanian Parliament Moves Toward Nuclear Ban Reversal as Baltic Provocations Heat Up SIMPLICIUS SEP 26, 2026 T he number of odd “happenings” is growing in the Baltics each day, as the specter of a broader conflict continues to haunt Europe. Each week brings new alarming signals of false flags and psyops which make it clear that provocations are constantly being prepared and trial-ballooned by Western intel agencies. Latvia says its eastern border surveillance system is being deliberately sabotaged, with cables cut and equipment cabinets damaged along the Russian and Belarusian borders. Officials blame growing provocations backed by the "aggressor state" — Faytuks Network (@FaytuksNetwork) September 26, 2026 Another scare was drummed up when news came that Russian FSB imposed “temporary border crossing restrictions” on two sections of the Estonian border: Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) has imposed temporary movement restrictions in two districts across the border from Estonia. The border directorate of the FSB’s St. Petersburg and Leningrad Oblast branch said measures would be in place in border areas of the Slantsy and Kingisepp districts from September 16–26 to “prevent violations of border and migration regulations” and “protect aquatic biological resources.” During this period, small vessels are prohibited from traveling on the section of the Narva River between the Bolshaya Cheryomukha and Kryusha (Krivasoo) rivers. It all sounds very perfunctory, but alas, the elites need a reason to sow fear. In Latvia, signs leading to Moscow were effaced: https://www.greanvillepost.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Lithuanian-Parliament-Moves-Toward-Nuclear-Ban-Reversal-as-Balti6.mp4 Moscow erased from road signs in Latvia Unknown individuals have painted over the names of Russian cities on road signs along Latvia’s A12 highway near Rezekne. The names covered were Moscow and Ostrov, a town in the Pskov region. The A12 is the main route from Latvia to the Russian border at Terehova, where it continues as the M9 highway to Moscow. But the biggest events have revolved around Lithuania. Just last week an air alert was issued in Vilnius after an alleged drone incursion. NATO fighter jets were then scrambled to shoot down the drone in what appeared to be a clear exercise meant to psychologically prime the citizens of Lithuania for the eventuality of a conflict that is much-needed for European elites. "A drone that just entered Lithuanian airspace was destroyed by NATO fighter jets. I thank Allied personnel for their swift response. With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine, such readiness is vital for our region. Together with our NATO Allies, Lithuania will defend its airspace," said Nausėda. The “drone” allegedly came from Belarus and was headed toward Russia’s Kaliningrad before NATO fighter jets valiantly swooped in to save their most worthy citizens from Putin’s aerial tyranny. Now Lithuania is trumpeting news of major evacuation plans in case of war with Russia: Lithuania, together with Poland developing the international population of the escape plan, which would be applied, where appropriate, across the border to evacuate part of the Lithuanian, Latvian and Estonian population. The national crisis management centre (NKVC) director Vilmanto Vitkausko according to the, currently, together with colleagues in Poland assessed procedures, logistics and infrastructure opportunities, and the plan should be drawn up by agreement between the parties. As is usual, however, it is Lithuania itself that is pushing the escalations. Lithuania’s parliament backed a preliminary proposal this week to remove the constitutional ban on nuclear weapons so that it could potentially host American nukes on its territory for “protection”: The logic behind the move: “We are the only country in the region that has this restriction. Latvia does not have it, Estonia does not have it, Poland does not have it, Finland has just removed it,” Kasčiūnas said. The official state media outlet Ria Novosti published an interesting article which it quickly took down afterwards, citing that it “did not align with the editorial team’s views” or state policy of Russia: Luckily, we have the internet archives: The piece, however, makes a rational case for why Russia would potentially need to dismantle Lithuania. The author argues that “France and the UK no longer hide their plans to deploy [nukes] in the Russian border region” and that: “The purpose of their involvement with the Baltic states is the same as it was last decade with the Ukrainians: to create an unacceptable level of security threats on Russia’s borders, which will force Moscow to take action.” The author goes on: One can hardly find fault in his reasoning. To build on that, Medvedev had a quite characteristic response to these Lithuanian developments: view full-width video-player-with-background video-player-wrapper full-width" role="region" aria-label="Video player"> Beyond the bit of grandstanding, Medvedev makes quite an important realist point: that if Russia were to attack Lithuania, or any of the Baltic poodles for that matter, no one would step in to save them. That’s because, not only is NATO in general at its weakest and most fractured ever, but also that the hallowed Article Five itself is mostly illusory. This week, head commissar of the NATO politburo Mark Rutte himself admitted that Article Five does not infact guarantee any sort of defense. He attempted his best to frame it in a way that sounds flattering, as if the “ambiguity” in the language redounds to NATO’s putative “strength”, when in reality it’s a desperate attempt to downplay the fact that Article Five was never the iron guarantee it’s made out to be: Putin also responded to the Estonian defense minister’s statement that Estonia is “ready to kill every Russian who crosses the border.” Putin stated that the Russian Army’s size alone is 1.5+ million to the 1.3 million of the entire Estonian population: He leaves us with another classic quote: “The circus left but the clowns stayed behind.” The various claims that Russia is preparing to invade Europe also give us something important to ponder. The Europeans are essentially admitting that Russia must have massive reserve forces available for this task, which means that Russian losses cannot possibly be as high as they claim if Russia is able to build up these rear forces in preparation for such an invasion. On the plus side, the German Foreign Ministry decided to meet with their Russian counterpart for the first time in close to five years—the last such dialogue took place just before the war in January, 2022. However, the meeting was another attempt by the West to pontificate and dictate terms to Russia, as Lavrov explained : "When we met, I invited him to lay out the purpose of his visit. He took out his notes and read a text that was a verbatim repetition of what German leaders state officially and publicly on a daily basis. That is essentially what Mr. Wadephul told me. I gleaned nothing new from it. The subtext was something like: "I came to see you—I deigned to engage with you—so now, in return for this 'gesture of goodwill' on my part, you need to make concessions on the Ukrainian front and ensure an agreement regarding the Black Sea region so that tankers and dry-cargo ships can pass through without issues." Lavrov went on to rightly call the European preparations for war a “self-fulfilling prophecy”: https://www.greanvillepost.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Lithuanian-Parliament-Moves-Toward-Nuclear-Ban-Reversal-as-Balti2.mp4 Reportedly, during the meeting the puckish Russian FM left a copy of a Russian report titled “Heirs of Goebbels” on the table for the German Foreign Ministry to enjoy: https://www.greanvillepost.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Lithuanian-Parliament-Moves-Toward-Nuclear-Ban-Reversal-as-Balti7.mp4 During his meeting with his German counterpart Wadephul Russian foriegn Minister Sergey Lavrov left copies of the Russian MFA report "Heirs of Goebbels" challenging the so called "Bucha massacre" on the table. The German minister covered it up with his notebook. Meanwhile, back in German FM Johann Wadephul’s home mass protests broke out over the new proposal to re-institute “voluntary” conscription in preparation for the inevitable: Imagine if these protests were happening in Russia over the SMO, the West would have already declared “Putin’s regime” to be facing internal revolt and collapse. In Estonia, the youth are likewise being prepared for things to come by being brainwashed to intensely hate Russia: German FM Wadephul’s admission that he broke a long-standing omerta against speaking to Russia for the sake of begging Russia for concessions on things like the Black Sea grain transport for Ukraine is very telling. It is another in a long line of recent examples showing Western desperation to save Ukraine at any cost. They couch the unfolding disaster in the framing that Russia is “stuck” and forced to somehow act out to depict Ukraine’s rapid decline as merely the result of Russian “weakness”. But we know that judging by Western politicians’ crony-like urgency of late, the situation is not as they present it. NYT writes: Hilariously, in only the second paragraph they falsify their own article framing by admitting that Russia only began blowing up Ukraine’s economy after Ukraine started doing it first, rather than because Russia is “stuck on the battlefield”: Oops. It’s funny how Western rags inadvertently tie themselves into logical knots when fumbling over their own clumsy propaganda. After the above contradiction, they further state that a stalemated war turns to a battle of economic attrition. Yet they go on to admit that Russia is winning the attrition. So, if a war whose frontline has “ground to a halt” is thereby decided by economic attrition, and Russia is winning that economic attrition by a country mile, are we not to assume that the war is thus not “stalemated” at all, but is in fact being won by Russia? They try in any way possible to torture out some convoluted logic by which Ukraine could be perceived as “not losing”, when all their own data and conjectures clearly adduce precisely the opposite. Good ol’ Western rags and their 4-dimensional meta-logic. Ukraine is both suffering the lion’s share of losses and destruction, but somehow winning. Russia is both losing and has no men to ply a “deadlocked” battlefield, yet is ready to invade Europe from every direction with an unstoppable phantom army. Also, if Putin’s “stuck army” is being contained and slaughtered piecemeal in Ukraine, wouldn’t a ceasefire be the most dangerous possible outcome, as it would free his “stuck soldiers” to come invade Europe? Yet it is the Europeans who are desperate to freeze the “already stuck” Russian Army along the current line of contact, and free it to potentially march elsewhere. Things that make you go hmm. (If your IQ’s higher than your diastolic pressure, that is.) Virtually none of the logic out of the dim-witted Euro-circus can any longer even pass the sanity test.
